title: Finite Smith–Toda Complexes at Varying Primes
main_claim: For every n ≥ 0 there exist a prime p and a finite p-local spectrum X with BP_*X ≅ BP_*/(p,v_1,…,v_n) as comodules (a Smith–Toda complex V(n)). The proof works in the ultraproduct over p of p-local spectra, with sphere degrees that vary with p. Successive attaching classes come from a Tate-type p-fold permutation power over C_p⋊F_p^×, normalized by an Euler class. A universal Koszul coefficient algebra, connectivity estimates at weights that grow with p, and Amitsur completion supply the normalization. Detection uses a Borel MU p-series relation, and finitely many maps and homotopies then descend to a single prime.

issues.description: The proof works for an arbitrary nonprincipal ultrafilter U, so it actually implies that V(n) exists for all but finitely many primes. That is a much stronger statement than the theorem as written, and a major claim (the paper itself notes V(4) was open at every prime). It is not an error, but given how strong the result is, the deep homotopical inputs need an expert check. I could only check them for plausibility.
issues.evidence: Suppose the set of primes where the construction works had infinite complement. Choose U containing that complement; Sec. 8 then gives a U-large set of good primes, which is a contradiction. The finite descent in Prop. ultraproduct and real:hurewicz needs only a U-large set.

issues.location: Lemmas layer:partial-thom, layer:coefficient-algebra, layer:odd-vanishing; Lemma power:exactness
issues.description: The identification B(1)//t ≃ Q⊗D//ϖ depends on the localization E being built from bounded join stages and taking the ultraproduct before the colimit over b. At any single prime J^∨ is induced and its Tate construction vanishes; the nonzero layer D/ϖ appears only because of this order of limits. I checked the cell and group-homology arguments for fixed b and large p, and the norm composite p(p-1). Still, this is the most delicate and least standard step, and I could not verify every coherence claim (for example the multiplicativity of the layer comparison).
issues.evidence: Part(T^r Z) for even r equals the underlying spectrum because H_*(G;F_p) vanishes in degrees 1 through 2p-4. Full(J^∨Z) ≅ Z because S(V)_{hG} is p-locally acyclic (checked: the F_p^×-invariants of Λ(η)⊗F_p[ξ]/ξ^{(p-1)/2} sit in degree 0 only).

coverage:
Read all nine sections (about 4100 lines of LaTeX), checking computations by hand.

Verified:
- Sec. 5 connectivity: the Sylow and normalizer description of H^*(Σ_k) for k<p^2; the multiplier-weight degrees 2p-3 (even case) and p-2 (twisted case); the kernel of restriction (V^{⊗l})^{Σ_l} giving the T_{p,k} bound; the per-generator inequality -r+1_{odd}+2·1_{r=0} ≥ 2(1-r) together with ν(γ_{j,S}) = 1-|S|; the degree-gap arithmetic 2p(ν(λ)+m) - 2m + 2ν(δ) - E - s.
- Sec. 6: the logic of the Amitsur K-local completion; t becoming an equivalence for m > -ν(λ); target locality via derived t-completeness.
- Sec. 7: the leading term of the Hazewinkel p-series; k_u ∈ I_h for u < p^h; the ε²-divisibility argument through the invariant range p ≤ s < 2p-2; ideal-order bookkeeping in the coefficient extraction (terms with u > p^a give pu - p^{a+1} ≥ p; terms with s ≥ 2 land in I_{a+1}²).
- Sec. 8: t-injectivity from evenness; term-by-term mapping of the cobordism relation; cancelling t and reducing mod t; the descent step.
- Sec. 2: the a_2-null connectivity bound 2(p-1)-(p-2) = p.

Accepted as plausible but not independently verified: the higher-categorical coherence claims (rectification, finite-cell Morita equivalence, Picard grading) and the layer comparison.
